instruction: Out of all the subjects that you can study at the University of Cambridge, which ones saw an increase in the percentage of acceptances of students from Maintained schools between the 2019 and 2021 undergraduate admissions cycles and then also between the 2021 and 2023 undergraduate admissions cycles. Consider Home applicants only.
answer:
Now I have all the data needed. Let me compile the analysis from the three official Cambridge admissions statistics reports.

## Subjects with Increased Maintained School Acceptance % in Both Periods (2019→2021 and 2021→2023)

Based on the official University of Cambridge Undergraduate Admissions Statistics reports for the 2019, 2021, and 2023 cycles (Home applicants only), **9 subjects** saw an increase in the percentage of acceptances from Maintained schools across both periods:

| Subject | 2019 | 2021 | 2023 | Change 2019→2021 | Change 2021→2023 |
|---------|------|------|------|------------------|------------------|
| **Anglo-Saxon, Norse, & Celtic** | 53.3% | 58.3% | 62.5% | +5.0pp | +4.2pp |
| **Archaeology** | 68.8% | 80.0% | 84.6% | +11.2pp | +4.6pp |
| **Economics** | 59.8% | 66.7% | 69.6% | +6.9pp | +2.9pp |
| **History** | 60.8% | 71.5% | 73.1% | +10.7pp | +1.6pp |
| **History of Art** | 45.5% | 57.1% | 57.7% | +11.6pp | +0.6pp |
| **Land Economy** | 70.4% | 72.7% | 73.2% | +2.3pp | +0.5pp |
| **Theology, Religion & Philosophy of Religion** | 55.6% | 67.6% | 68.6% | +12.0pp | +1.0pp |
| **Computer Science** | 76.5% | 77.9% | 82.1% | +1.4pp | +4.2pp |
| **Natural Sciences** | 68.9% | 72.0% | 74.0% | +3.1pp | +2.0pp |

### Notes
- All percentages refer to **Home applicants** accepted from **Maintained schools** (UK state-funded schools including comprehensives, grammars, sixth form colleges, and FE colleges) as a proportion of total Home acceptances from UK schools/colleges.
- Data sourced from Table 4.3 (2019), Table 1.2 (2021), and Table 2.2 (2023) of the respective admissions statistics reports.
- Cambridge defines "Home" as applicants permanently resident in the UK, and "Maintained" as UK state-funded schools/colleges (academies counted as comprehensive if non-selective, grammar if selective) [1][2][3].
- The 2021 cycle was affected by COVID-19 (noted in the 2021 report), but the methodology for school-type classification remained consistent across all three years.

## Sources
1. University of Cambridge, *Undergraduate Admissions Statistics – 2019 cycle*, Table 4.3: https://www.undergraduate.study.cam.ac.uk/sites/default/files/publications/ug_admissions_statistics_2019_cycle_0.pdf
2. University of Cambridge, *Undergraduate Admissions Statistics – 2021 cycle*, Table 1.2: https://www.undergraduate.study.cam.ac.uk/sites/default/files/publications/ug_admissions_statistics_2021_cycle.pdf
3. University of Cambridge, *Undergraduate Admissions Statistics – 2023 cycle*, Table 2.2: https://www.undergraduate.study.cam.ac.uk/sites/default/files/publications/ug_admissions_statistics_2023_cycle.pdf
